> I couldn't figure out how this boolean should work.

Something like this should be at the beginning of `NOTIFICATION_DRAW`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ecfe34f56cd991f729b813a94df117dd8e6ab31f/scene/2d/physics/touch_screen_button.cpp#L140-L142

This should also be done where input is processed, so that input is skipped if the button is invisible because the user doesn't have a touchscreen currently.

You've accidentally merged the master branch into your branch incorrectly taking ownership over the changes, to prevent this make sure you rebase to update your branch, to fix this you need to remove the merge commit with master and rebase instead, see [here](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/organization/pull_requests/creating_pull_requests.html#the-interactive-rebase)
Is it now fixed?

This patch introduces the `touchscreen_only` and puts some juicy code behind that flag.

On touch devices, it would be great if buttons responded to screen taps, without having to rely on "emulate mouse from touch", as it is not always possible to set that flag without interfering with other things.

So I think that the touchscreen_only makes sense as a feature, but the code that processes events should still process it for cases where touchscreen_only is not set, for folks that just added a button and wanted the button to work without flipping a switch that might conflict.

> So I think that the touchscreen_only makes sense as a feature, but the code that processes events should still process it for cases where touchscreen_only is not set, for folks that just added a button and wanted the button to work without flipping a switch that might conflict.

So you need still have `Emulate Mouse from Touch` enabled since most `Control` Nodes just using `Mouse Events`.

> But selecting the Option is internally handled by the `PopupMenu` which depends on `Mouse Events`. So you need still have `Emulate Mouse from Touch` enabled since most `Control` Nodes just using `Mouse Events`.

> Do we want to have a hover if the touch started outside and dragged inside the button?
Hover test, Video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55f16671-2685-4ad1-9e30-11ea68017cd1
I believe the following bug fix is ​​needed to solve it properly. Only after that is it possible to receive `InputEventScreenTouch`, when the finger inside the button is no longer touching the touchscreen. ```cpp if (!over) { over = gui_find_control(pos); } ``` here in the `Viewport`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/main/viewport.cpp#L2238-L2251 It still needs to be checked whether this change leads to regressions. **EDIT:** A safer/better solution would probably be to force an `InputEventScreenDrag`event with pressed = false (if possible) instead. What also doesn't work yet is the multitouch hover effect; a maximum of 1 button changes the hover status.
Do we even want to have a hovering for touch input, since hovering is technically not possible with a touch input.
I agree that it makes little sense to give touches a hovering state.

I just want to offer a rebuttal that there are touch inputs that support hovering.

For example, I plan to use multitouch support for XR finger input, and in XR you have full 6 degree of freedom information about the finger locations at all times when using hand tracking.

Also, tablets with a pen and stylus often show the hover location of the stylus. it's not multi-touch, but it is a form of touch input.

I'm not here to block this on hover support for touch input, just trying to make a case that there are applications (such as my VR framework) that may have a use for hover.
Maybe we could add hovering for touch input in a follow up pull request. Currently i don't have a device to test it.
